{{short description|American basketball player (born 2001)}} {{Use American English|date=June 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=July 2024}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Julian Champagnie | image = Julian Champagnie San Antonio Spurs 2024.jpg | image_size = | caption = Champagnie with the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in 2024 | team = San Antonio Spurs | number = 30 | position = [[Power forward]] | league = [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 7 | weight_lb = 217 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2001|6|29}} | birth_place = [[Brooklyn, New York]], U.S. | high_school = [[Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School|Bishop Loughlin]]
(Brooklyn, New York) | college = [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] (2019–2022) | draft_year = 2022 | career_start = 2022 | years1 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team1 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years2 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2022–2023]] | team2 = →[[Delaware Blue Coats]] | years3 = {{nbay|2022|end}}–present | team3 = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | years4 = [[2022-23 NBA G League season|2023]] | team4 = →[[Austin Spurs]] | highlights = * 2× First-team [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big East]] (2021, 2022) * [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Most Improved Player|Big East co-Most Improved Player]] (2021) * Big East All-Freshman Team (2020) }} '''Julian Kymani Champagnie''' ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|ʃ|ae|m|'|p|ɛ|n|i|}} {{respell|sham|PEH|nee}}; born June 29, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]], where he was a two-time [[List of All-Big East Conference men's basketball teams|first-team All-Big East selection]] and led the conference in scoring in 2021. After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Champagnie began his career on a two-way contract with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. He was claimed off waivers by the Spurs in February 2023 and subsequently signed a standard multi-year contract. He established himself as a core piece of the Spurs' rotation, setting the Spurs' single-season franchise record for made three-pointers during the 2025–26 regular season and helping San Antonio reach the [[2026 NBA Finals]].{{cite news |last1=Guzman |first1=Matt |title=How Julian Champagnie Shot His Way into San Antonio Spurs' History Books |url=https://www.si.com/nba/spurs/onsi/news/how-julian-champagnie-shot-his-way-into-san-antonio-spurs-history-books |access-date=May 30, 2026 |work=Sports Illustrated |date=April 6, 2026}} ==Early life== Champagnie was born in [[Staten Island|Staten Island, New York]] and grew up in [[Kensington|Brooklyn, New York]] and attended [[Bishop Loughlin Memorial High School]], where he played alongside his twin brother, [[Justin Champagnie|Justin]]. He averaged 15 points as a junior, earning Third Team All-[[Catholic High School Athletic Association]] (CHSAA) AA honors. As a senior, Champagnie averaged 17.2 points and was named to the First Team All-CHSAA AA.{{cite web |last1=Mancari |first1=Jim |title=Bishop Loughlin Star Stays Home at St. John's |url=https://thetablet.org/bishop-loughlin-star-at-st-johns/ |website=[[The Tablet (Brooklyn)|The Tablet]] |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=June 19, 2019}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] over offers from [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]], [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State]], [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] and [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]].{{cite web |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=St. John's sends message with local Julian Champagnie commit |url=https://nypost.com/2019/05/30/st-johns-sends-message-with-local-julian-champagnie-commit/ |website=[[New York Post]] |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=May 30, 2019}} ==College career== On March 4, 2020, Champagnie recorded a freshman season-high 23 points and six rebounds in a 77–55 loss to [[Butler Bulldogs men's basketball|Butler]].{{cite web |title=St. John's Falls to Butler, 77-55 |url=https://redstormsports.com/news/2020/3/4/mens-basketball-st-johns-falls-to-butler-77-55.aspx |website=St. John's University Athletics |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=March 4, 2020}} In his next game, three days later, he posted 21 points and 12 rebounds in an 88–86 win over [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]].{{cite web |title=Champagnie, Rutherford help St. John's beat Marquette 88-86 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168422 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=March 7, 2020}} As a freshman, Champagnie averaged 9.9 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Venter |first1=Alicia |title=Back for more: Julian Champagnie is coming in confident |url=https://www.torchonline.com/sports/2020/11/13/back-for-more-julian-champagnie-is-coming-in-confident/ |website=[[The Torch (St. John's University)|The Torch]] |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=November 13, 2020}} He was a two-time [[Big East Conference|Big East]] Freshman of the Week and an All-Freshman Team selection.{{cite web |last1=Harkins |first1=Lukas |title=St. John's Basketball: Julian Champagnie poised for stardom in 2020-21 |url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2020/05/26/st-johns-basketball-julian-champagnie-poised-stardom-2020-21/ |website=Busting Brackets |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=May 26, 2020}} On November 30, 2020, Champagnie made his sophomore season debut, recording 29 points and 10 rebounds in a 97–93 win over [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]].{{cite web |title=St. John's holds off BC behind Champagnie's 29 points |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/basketball-ncaa-boc-stjn/st-johns-holds-off-bc-behind-champagnies-29-points-idUSMTZXEGC1N0LYXJ |website=[[Reuters]] |publisher=Field Level Media |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=November 30, 2020}} On January 9, 2021, he tallied 33 points and 10 rebounds in a 97–79 loss to seventh-ranked [[Creighton Bluejays men's basketball|Creighton]], the first 30-point [[double-double]] by a St. John's player since [[D'Angelo Harrison]] in 2015.{{cite web |last1=Rubin |first1=Roger |title=St. John's falls behind early, crushed by Creighton |url=https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/st-johns/st-john-s-red-storm-creighton-t06219 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210112040026/https://www.newsday.com/sports/college/st-johns/st-john-s-red-storm-creighton-1.50114558 |url-status=live |archive-date=January 12, 2021 |website=[[Newsday]] |access-date=January 20, 2021 |date=January 10, 2021}} As a sophomore, Champagnie averaged 19.8 points, 7.4 rebounds, 1.4 steals and one block per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility. However, on July 4, 2021, he announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning to St. John's for his junior year.{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Julian Champagnie returning to St. John's after testing NBA Draft waters |url=https://nypost.com/2021/07/04/2021-nba-draft-julian-champagnie-returning-to-st-johns/ |access-date=October 20, 2021 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=July 4, 2021}} On January 5, 2022, he scored a career-high 34 points in a 89–84 win over [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]]. As a junior, Champagnie averaged 19.2 points, 6.6 rebounds, two steals and 1.1 blocks per game. He was named to the First Team All-Big East as a junior for the second consecutive season.{{cite news |last1=Braziller |first1=Zach |title=Julian Champagnie named to Big East first team to join exclusive St. John's club |url=https://nypost.com/2022/03/07/st-johns-julian-champagnie-on-big-east-first-team-again/ |access-date=March 10, 2022 |work=[[New York Post]] |date=March 7, 2022}} On April 2, 2022, Champagnie declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility. He ultimately went undrafted.{{Cite news|url=https://stormthepaint.com/2022/06/24/st-johns-basketball-champagnie-undrafted/|title=St. John's basketball: Julian Champagnie not selected in 2022 NBA Draft|work=stormthepaint.com|author=Kevin Connelly|date=June 24, 2022|accessdate=June 24, 2022}} ==Professional career== ===Philadelphia 76ers (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], on June 24, 2022, Champagnie signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Lucas |date=June 24, 2022 |title=Sixers add undrafted rookie Julian Champagnie to two-way deal |url=https://thesixersense.com/2022/06/24/sixers-add-undrafted-rookie-julian-champagnie-two-way-deal/ |access-date=June 24, 2022 |website=The Sixer Sense}} He made two appearances for Philadelphia during his rookie campaign, recording one steal and no points. On February 14, 2023, Champagnie was waived by the 76ers.{{cite web |title=Mac McClung Signs Two-Way Contract with Philadelphia 76ers |url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/76ers-sign-mac-mcclung |access-date=February 14, 2023 |website=NBA}} ===San Antonio / Austin Spurs (2023–present)=== On February 16, 2023, the [[San Antonio Spurs]] claimed Champagnie off waivers and signed him to a two-way contract.{{Cite web|title=SPURS CLAIM JULIAN CHAMPAGNIE OFF WAIVERS|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-claim-julian-champagnie-off-waivers|website=NBA.com|date=February 16, 2023|access-date=February 16, 2023}} On July 6, 2023, Champagnie re-signed with the Spurs.{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/news/spurs-re-sign-julian-champagnie|title=SPURS RE-SIGN JULIAN CHAMPAGNIE|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2023}} On February 10, 2025, Julian played against his twin brother [[Justin Champagnie|Justin]] for the first time in an NBA game, when the Spurs met the [[Washington Wizards]]. {{Cite web|title=Oh, brother: As Champagnie twins have a moment, Spurs turn back Wizards|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2025/02/10/wizards-spurs-champagnie-twins/|website=washingtonpost.com|last=Shankar|first=Varun|date=February 11, 2025|access-date=February 11, 2025}} They are among a very small number of twins who have ever played against one another in an NBA game.{{Cite web|title=How many sets of twins have played in the NBA?|url=https://fansided.com/2023/06/22/how-many-sets-twins-nba-history//|website=fansided.com|date=June 22, 2023|last=Wilson|first=Josh|access-date=February 11, 2025}} Champagnie appeared in all 82 games for San Antonio during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 9.9 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.{{cite web | last=O'Donnell | first=Ricky | title=11 NBA iron men who played all 82 games this season, including an old and tiny Chris Paul | website=SB Nation | date=2025-04-14 | url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2025/4/14/24408190/nba-players-all-82-games-appear-ironman-chris-paul-mikal-bridges | access-date=2025-12-06}} On December 31, 2025, Champagnie scored a career-high 36 points off of 11 made three-point field goals in a victory over the [[2025–26 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]].{{Cite web |last=Quan |first=Gary |date=December 31, 2025 |title=San Antonio vs. New York, Final Score: Spurs mount comeback over Knicks 134-132 |url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/game-recaps/92314/san-antonio-vs-new-york-final-score-spurs-mount-comeback-over-knicks-134-132 |access-date=January 1, 2026 |website=Pounding the Rock}} His 11 three-pointers also set a Spurs franchise record for the most three-pointers made in a game. Champagnie went on to finish the 2025–26 regular season with 195 made three-pointers, the most in a single season in Spurs franchise history.{{cite web |url=https://unitedsportsdesk.com/julian-champagnies-spurs-all-time-three-pointer-record-2026-turns-a-breakout-season-into-franchise-history/ |title=Julian Champagnie's Spurs all time three pointer record 2026 turns a breakout season into franchise history |website=United Sports Desk |date=May 7, 2026 |access-date=May 10, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://fieldlevelmedia.com/nba/nba-roundup-julian-champagnie-11-treys-leads-spurs-past-knicks/|title=NBA roundup: Julian Champagnie (11 treys) leads Spurs past Knicks|website=Field Level Media|date=January 1, 2026|access-date=January 1, 2026}} He would end up playing in all 82 games for San Antonio (starting 68), averaging 11.1 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 1.5 assists (all career-highs).{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}} On June 29, 2026, Champagnie re-signed with the Spurs on a three-year, $45 million contract.{{Cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |date=June 29, 2026 |title=Sources: Julian Champagnie to sign 3-year, $45M deal with Spurs |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49219150/sources-julian-champagnie-sign-3-year-45m-deal-spurs |access-date=June 30, 2026 |website=espn.com |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player raised in [[Kensington, Brooklyn]].
